# Publish partial work as a draft PR, and refuse workflow-file changes

One part of the GitHub Actions workflow work. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below. Don't assume access to any other issue or to `docs/specs/github-actions-workflow.md`.

**Order:** builds on `jig github implement`, which already opens a ready PR for a completed run and comments when nothing changed.

## What

When a run started from an issue cannot finish but did produce changes, jig opens a **draft** PR. One PR comment lists what is still open: the reviewer's unresolved findings, final-check gaps and verification failures. If the run's changes touch anything under `.github/workflows/`, jig publishes nothing and explains on the issue that this automation cannot change workflows.

## Why

Attempts cost time and money. A run that ran out of attempts often leaves useful work and the exact list of what is wrong; throwing both away means a person starts from zero. Workflow files decide what runs with the repository's credentials, so the automation must never ship changes to them.

## Context

jig is a Node CLI (TypeScript, Vitest) that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has one agent implement and another review each slice inside a Docker sandbox, and lands them on one run branch, `jig/run/<id>`. Before editing, read `README.md`, `docs/architecture.html`, `CLAUDE.md`, and every `.claude/rules/` file that covers a file you will change, specs included.

The layering is domain rules (`src/domain/`) → flows and steps (`src/flow/`, `src/steps/`) → ports (`src/ports/`) → adapters (`src/adapters/`). Composition lives in `src/app/` and commands in `src/cli/`. Specs sit beside the code as `*.spec.ts` and pass fakes for ports, never module mocks. Anything that touches git is tested against a real temporary repository (`tests/support/temp-repo.ts`).

This issue is one part of the GitHub Actions workflow. In that workflow an operator marks GitHub issues ready, and jig, running in GitHub Actions under a GitHub App identity, implements them, opens PRs and works on review feedback. The jig core, called the *execution engine* (plan, implement, verify, review), stays independent of GitHub. The GitHub code is an *integration*: optional, jig-owned code in its own directory (`src/integrations/github/` unless one already exists). It depends on core contracts, and the core never imports it. jig must start without the integration or its credentials.

- `jig github implement --issue <n>` exists, with its GitHub port, orchestration state ref and publication receipts.
- Run state records why a run stopped: which cap was hit, on which slice, after how many attempts (`src/domain/run-state.ts`, `result.json`).
- Review feedback is free text today (`src/steps/slice.ts`); final-check results live in `src/domain/final-check.ts`.

## Target

- An outcome of `stuck` with commits on the run branch beyond the starting commit opens a draft PR (same head, base and body rules as a ready PR) plus one PR-level comment with the remaining findings, final-check gaps and the last verification failure.
- Findings are published **at PR level only**. Keep any file and line a finding mentions as text, and never invent an inline anchor. Inline placement is a later issue.
- Before any publication, check the change set (default branch fork point to run head). Any added, modified or deleted path under `.github/workflows/` means: publish nothing, comment on the issue naming the files, and record the refusal in orchestration state.
- The comment is repeatable without duplicates, through a receipt in orchestration state.

## Don't undo these

- **Agents and project commands run only inside the sandbox.** Never on the runner host, not even "for CI".
- **Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line, the image, or the sandbox.** The App key and the publishing token stay in the host process.
- **The core never imports the GitHub integration.** Dependencies point from the integration toward core contracts.
- **The host publishes, not the sandbox.** Pushes, PRs and comments are made by the GitHub integration in the host process.
- **No automatic merge.** A person merges every PR. `mergeMode` does not apply to runs this automation starts.

## Done when

- [ ] A stuck run with commits opens one draft PR and one findings comment; a rerun adds neither again
- [ ] A stuck run with no commits opens no PR and comments on the issue
- [ ] A run that changes `.github/workflows/ci.yml` publishes nothing and the issue comment names the file
- [ ] `npm run validate` passes from the repository root


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/14

# Add `jig github setup` and a manual-dispatch workflow for personal repositories

One part of the GitHub Actions workflow work. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below. Don't assume access to any other issue or to `docs/specs/github-actions-workflow.md`.

## What

A new command writes a GitHub Actions workflow into the target repository for the operator to review and commit. With it, the operator starts `jig github implement` for an issue by hand from the Actions tab. The workflow installs a pinned jig release from the package registry, runs on a Docker-capable runner and acts as a GitHub App. New documentation walks through setup on a personal GitHub account, with no organization, paid plan or hosted service.

## Why

Without a workflow and setup steps, `jig github implement` only runs from someone's laptop. Each repository has to be able to use it without a checkout of jig's source, and jig's own repository is just the first one.

## Context

jig is a Node CLI (TypeScript, Vitest) that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has one agent implement and another review each slice inside a Docker sandbox, and lands them on one run branch, `jig/run/<id>`. Before editing, read `README.md`, `docs/architecture.html`, `CLAUDE.md`, and every `.claude/rules/` file that covers a file you will change, specs included.

The layering is domain rules (`src/domain/`) → flows and steps (`src/flow/`, `src/steps/`) → ports (`src/ports/`) → adapters (`src/adapters/`). Composition lives in `src/app/` and commands in `src/cli/`. Specs sit beside the code as `*.spec.ts` and pass fakes for ports, never module mocks. Anything that touches git is tested against a real temporary repository (`tests/support/temp-repo.ts`).

This issue is one part of the GitHub Actions workflow. In that workflow an operator marks GitHub issues ready, and jig, running in GitHub Actions under a GitHub App identity, implements them, opens PRs and works on review feedback. The jig core, called the *execution engine* (plan, implement, verify, review), stays independent of GitHub. The GitHub code is an *integration*: optional, jig-owned code in its own directory (`src/integrations/github/` unless one already exists). It depends on core contracts, and the core never imports it. jig must start without the integration or its credentials.

- `jig github implement --issue <n>` exists and publishes PRs, draft PRs and comments.
- `jig init` already writes files for the operator to review and commit (`.sandcastle/Dockerfile`, `jig.config.json`); follow its pattern. Nothing else in the target's tracked files may change.
- Releases are published to GitHub Packages by `.github/workflows/publish.yml`.
- `docs/authentication.md` covers agent credentials, including the Codex login cache that jig writes back.

## Recorded operator decisions

These decisions settle the authentication ambiguity that blocked saved run `add-jig-github-setup-and-a-manual-89ca2c32` at design-review finding F2. They are part of this request, not an instruction to skip design review.

- Use one dedicated GitHub App per target repository for this version. Create/install it only for that repository; configure its identity and private key in that repository's Actions configuration/secrets. Mint installation tokens explicitly scoped to that repository. No shared multi-repository App, central service, automatic App provisioning, or workflow-write permission is required.
- Existing agent-provider authentication is authorized inside the sandbox, limited to the allowlist under **Don't undo these**. GitHub authentication is excluded from that allowlist and stays host-only.
- Authenticate both host Git transport and GitHub API operations using the repository-scoped App identity. Passing a token only to Octokit is insufficient when checkout credential persistence is disabled. Include receipt/state fetches and pushes as well as run-branch publication. Use ephemeral host-only authentication without writing credentials to files or exposing them in command arguments, remote URLs, logs or sandbox inputs.

### Flow examples

```text
Configure repository A's dedicated App and selected provider authentication
Dispatch A's workflow for an issue
  -> host mints an installation token scoped to A
  -> host authenticates Git remote operations and GitHub API publication
  -> sandbox receives only the selected agents' allowlisted provider authentication
  -> agents implement inside the sandbox
  -> host publishes the branch and PR; a person reviews and merges
  -> uploaded logs contain neither GitHub nor provider credential values
```

```text
Choose supported Codex login-cache authentication
  -> use the established explicitly selected private cache copy
  -> permit valid refreshed credentials to be written back under the existing contract
  -> never include that cache in target context, generated workflow content, images or artifacts
  -> document provisioning and writeback limitations on ephemeral Actions runners
```

```text
Set up repository B
  -> configure B's own App and secrets
  -> A's GitHub credentials are never supplied to B or to either sandbox
```

## Target

- **`jig github setup`** writes the workflow from a versioned template that ships in the package. The generated file records its template version. jig refuses, with a clear message, a workflow whose template version it does not support.
- **The workflow** only maps the trigger (`workflow_dispatch` with an issue number) to the command and passes credentials. It runs from the default branch, installs the pinned jig version from the registry (never jig code from a checkout), mints a repository-scoped installation token with `actions/create-github-app-token`, and uploads jig's logs as an Actions artifact.
- **Trusted inputs:** the job takes `jig.config.json` and `.sandcastle/Dockerfile` from the default-branch commit it checked out, records that commit (the *trusted commit*) in the request, and uses it for the whole execution. The image build gets no credentials, and its build context holds only content from that commit.
- **`docs/github.md`**, linked from `docs/README.md`, covers:
  - creating the App on a personal account and its permissions: contents, pull requests and issues, never workflows
  - secrets
  - how the workflow authenticates to the registry for the pinned package
  - which agent login modes work on a runner that keeps no files between jobs, saying whether the Codex login cache works
  - Docker on the runner
  - runner and provider costs, kept separate from the fact that no paid plan is needed
  - upgrading the template and the pinned jig version
  - that installing the App alone sets up nothing

## Don't undo these

- **Agents and project commands run only inside the sandbox.** Never on the runner host, not even "for CI".
- **GitHub credentials stay host-only.** The GitHub App private key, installation/publishing tokens, and Git transport authentication must never enter sandbox environments, mounts, files, image/build inputs, prompts, logs or uploaded artifacts. Only host orchestration and publication may use them.
- **Agent credentials are explicitly allowlisted.** Retain jig's existing supported provider authentication for the selected agents: provider credentials injected as runtime environment variables and the documented private copy of an explicitly selected Codex login cache, including valid refresh writeback. This exception permits those agent credentials inside the sandbox; it does not permit unrelated host credentials, bulk environment forwarding, or GitHub credentials. Keep provider values out of prompts, logs, reports, images/build inputs and uploaded artifacts. Preserve the existing documented operator-approved `.jig/.env` behavior and private Codex-cache protections; do not introduce additional credential files or authentication mechanisms.
- **The core never imports the GitHub integration.** Dependencies point from the integration toward core contracts.
- **The host publishes, not the sandbox.** Pushes, PRs and comments are made by the GitHub integration in the host process.
- **No automatic merge.** A person merges every PR. `mergeMode` does not apply to runs this automation starts.

## Done when

- [ ] Boundary specs with sentinel credentials prove selected provider authentication remains usable through supported sandbox paths while GitHub credentials never reach sandbox/build inputs, prompts, files, logs or uploaded artifacts. Do not claim provider authentication is credential-free.
- [ ] Host Git and API publication both authenticate with the selected repository App when checkout credential persistence is disabled; permission scope and credential-free failure diagnostics are covered.

- [ ] Specs: setup writes the workflow with its template version; an unsupported version is refused; no other tracked file changes
- [ ] Opt-in live check, run by hand and described in `docs/testing.md`: in a disposable personal repository without jig's source, dispatching the workflow for an issue opens a PR, and the repository's ordinary CI runs on that PR
- [ ] `npm run validate` passes from the repository root



Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/15

# docs: add ownership guidance to house rules and the PR procedure

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

## What

Write down where each kind of code belongs, so contributors and agents put new code in the right
place without having to ask.

## Why

The upcoming restructuring moves code between owners. Unless the rules explain the reasoning,
later changes will drift back to the old layout.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Target responsibilities", "Error ownership and technical failure handling",
"House rules and review".

- `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md`, `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`,
  `.claude/rules/parse-input-at-the-edge.md`: add short ownership guidance with concrete examples:
  - CLI does not receive a container or cradle; it calls an application operation and presents the result.
  - Configurable defaults (for example the step retry count) are not domain rules; domain consumes
    resolved `RunSettings`.
  - A capability failure (storage, Git, sandbox) belongs with its port contract, not in domain just
    because several modules return it.
  - Composition only wires: it chooses implementations and starts the executable, and makes no
    resume, retry, locking or publication decisions.
- `.claude/skills/commit-pr/SKILL.md` and `.github/pull_request_template.md`: a PR that changes
  ownership states the owner, why the concept belongs there, and whether it introduces a pattern
  agents should copy. Add this to the existing procedure; do not create a parallel guide.
- Also update `.agents/` copies of these rules or skills if they exist and are tracked.

This issue changes documentation only. Do not move code, and do not enforce ownership through
names (such as `DEFAULT_*`) or tests that check prose.

## Done when

- [ ] The rules above carry the four examples, each in the rule that owns it.
- [ ] The PR procedure and template ask for an ownership rationale.
- [ ] `npm run format:check` and `npm run lint` pass.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/54

# refactor(config): split config I/O from policy and own retry defaults

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

## What

Settings files and the environment are still read the same way and give the same results, but the
code that decides what a setting means no longer reads files itself.

## Why

Configuration rules are mixed with file and directory access. That makes them hard to reuse from
anything other than the command line, and hard to test without a disk. Retry defaults also live with
business rules even though they are configurable values.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Configuration and defaults", "Application preparation and resource lifetime".

- `src/config/load-config.ts` (`loadConfig`, `configFileFor`), `src/config/presets.ts`
  (`discoverPresets`, `presetDirectories`, `loadPreset`), `src/config/write-config.ts`
  (`updateConfigFile`) and `src/config/environment.ts` mix schemas and resolution with file reads
  and writes, directory discovery and `process.env`.
- Config keeps the schemas, default values, provider/model policy, preset-name validation,
  precedence and selection. Move file reading and writing, and preset directory discovery, to
  adapters behind narrow capabilities (functions or small port interfaces). Environment capture
  moves to the process edge. Config parses the raw values it is given. Parse each input once, at its
  edge; never copy a schema into a caller.
- `src/domain/settings.ts` exports `MAX_STEP_RETRIES = 2` and `RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5000`, and
  `runSettingsFrom` in `load-config.ts` imports them. Move both to config-owned defaults with the
  same values. Domain keeps `RunSettings` and rules such as comparing review cycles with the
  resolved cap. Do not add operator overrides (separate work), and do not let presets set run settings.
- Do not move other caps just because they are numbers. Genuine safety and stopping rules stay in domain.
- Error classes stay where they are for now; a later issue reassigns them. Keep returning the same
  `ConfigInvalid` values.

## Done when

- [ ] No file under `src/config/` imports `node:fs` or reads `process.env`
      (`grep -rnE "node:fs|process\.env" src/config --include=*.ts | grep -v spec` finds nothing).
- [ ] `src/domain/settings.ts` no longer exports the retry defaults; config supplies 2 and 5000 ms.
- [ ] Existing config, preset and environment behavior tests pass. New tests cover the moved I/O
      through fakes or temporary directories.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/55

# refactor(config): read settings and presets through sources with no file-system vocabulary

**Treat this request as self-contained.** Everything needed is below; don't assume access to any other issue or pull request.

## What

Where jig gets its settings and its agent presets from becomes a detail that the settings rules never see. Today the settings rules talk in terms of files, folders and paths. After this change they talk only in terms of "the settings", "the presets" and their names, and the part that knows about files sits behind them. Nothing an operator sees changes.

## Why

The rules for what a valid setting or preset is should not care whether the text came from a file on disk, a password manager or standard input. Right now they do: the config module describes presets as files in directories, and the config-file reader applies the settings rules itself. That makes it unclear where checking happens, and every new place jig could read settings from would have to remember to apply the rules on its own. Keeping the rules on one side and the storage on the other means the rules run once, in one place, for every source.

## Context — read this first

jig is a Node/TypeScript CLI, tested with Vitest. Specs sit beside the code they cover (`load-config.ts` → `load-config.spec.ts`). Shared test fakes live in `tests/support/fakes.ts`, data builders in `tests/support/builders.ts`. Read `.claude/rules/` before editing, especially `callee-owns-its-rules.md`, `parse-input-at-the-edge.md`, `errors-as-values.md` and `testing-conventions.md`.

Layering that matters here:

- `src/config/` owns configuration **policy**: schemas, defaults, validation, preset name rules, precedence ("first found wins"), merging a preset into the config, and the merge rule for updates. A dependency-cruiser rule `config-does-no-io` in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` already forbids `src/config/` from importing `fs`, `os`, `src/adapters/` and `write-file-atomic`.
- `src/adapters/config/` does the disk work: `config-file.ts` (read and atomically update `jig.config.json` or a config named with `--config`) and `preset-files.ts` (find, list and read preset JSON files).
- `src/cli/with-app.ts` is the process edge. `processInvocation()` captures `process.env`, `cwd`, the OS home directory, and the concrete `readConfig` and `presetFiles` implementations. `src/app/container.ts` wires the same pieces for the app (`readConfig`, `updateConfig`, `presetFiles`). `src/app/init-sandbox.ts` reads and updates the config during `jig init`. `src/cli/commands/presets.ts` lists presets.

## The problem, concretely

**1. The config-file adapter applies config rules itself.** `readConfigFile` in `src/adapters/config/config-file.ts` reads the file, parses JSON, then calls `configFrom` and `mayBeAbsent` from `src/config/load-config.ts` and returns a finished `JigConfig`. `updateConfigFile` likewise calls `configWithSettings` from `src/config/update-config.ts`. Config rules are being applied from inside the adapter, so any second config source would have to repeat them.

**2. File-system words live in `src/config/`.**

- `ConfigFile { path, name, named }`, `configFileFor(repoRoot, preset?)` (uses `node:path`) and `mayBeAbsent(file)` in `src/config/load-config.ts`.
- The `PresetFiles` interface in `src/config/presets.ts`, with `directories(roots)`, `filesIn(directory)`, `fileFor(directory, name)`, `isPresent(path)` and `read(path)`. `presets.ts` walks the disk step by step through it.
- `PresetRoots`, `PresetDirectory`, `presetDirectories()` and `presetRoots()` (uses `path.isAbsolute` to accept only an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) in `src/config/presets.ts`.
- `PRESET_SOURCES = ['repository', 'home', 'xdg', 'builtin']` in `src/config/presets.ts`. These are disk locations, and their order is the disk layout's priority.

## Target shape

The settings and presets code asks a **source** for raw data in its own vocabulary, and applies the rules itself.

- **Config source.** `src/config/` declares what it needs from a config source: read its raw JSON (or "nothing there"), write raw JSON, and a human label for messages (today the file name, e.g. `jig.config.json`). `loadConfig(source, …)` in config reads the raw value and runs `configFrom`. Updating the config is read raw → `configWithSettings` → write raw, with the merge in config. The adapter only reads, parses and atomically writes JSON.
- **"Must exist" stays a config rule.** Today a missing default `jig.config.json` means `{}`, while a missing config the operator named with `--config` is a `ConfigInvalid`. The source reports "nothing there"; config decides what that means based on whether the operator chose it explicitly.
- **Preset source.** `src/config/` declares what it needs from presets: list the candidates (name, a source label such as `repository`, a location label such as the file path, and a way to read the candidate's raw JSON), and find the first candidate for one name. Candidates come back in the source's own priority order. Config validates names, keeps the first candidate per name, validates the JSON against the preset schema, and merges.
- **Disk layout moves to the adapter.** The four directories, their priority order (repository → home → xdg → builtin), `.json` file names, symlink-aware presence checks, the absolute-only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` rule and the path of the config file all belong to the file-system adapter. `src/config/` keeps none of `ConfigFile`, `configFileFor`, `mayBeAbsent`, `PresetFiles`, `PresetRoots`, `PresetDirectory`, `presetDirectories` or `PRESET_SOURCES` in their current file-shaped form.
- **Adapters are named by technology.** The adapter implements the config's interfaces for the file system; its name and location say "file system", not "config file" or "preset files". Choose names that fit `src/adapters/`.

Exact interface names, method names and file names are yours to choose. What must hold is: no file-system vocabulary in `src/config/`, adapters return raw (unvalidated) data, and every rule runs in config.

## Behaviour that must not change

Everything below is observable today and must still hold. Keep or move the specs that cover it; don't delete coverage.

- A missing default `jig.config.json` yields defaults from `{}`. A missing config named with `--config` fails with `ConfigInvalid`. Messages keep their current wording.
- A config that is not valid JSON, or not a JSON object when updating, fails with the current `ConfigInvalid` messages. Updates keep every key the operator wrote, including ones jig doesn't know, and are written atomically with `write-file-atomic`.
- Preset precedence is repository (`.jig/presets/` in the repo) → `~/.jig/presets/` → `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jig/presets/` (only when absolute, else `~/.config/jig/presets/`) → the packaged `presets/` starters. A directory shared by two sources is searched once.
- **Loading one preset by name reads only that preset.** A broken, unrelated preset elsewhere must not stop `--preset <name>`.
- **A broken higher-priority preset does not fall through** to a lower-priority one with the same name; it fails.
- A file whose name is not a valid preset name is ignored, never read.
- A missing preset fails with `No preset named <name> — looked in <locations>; available: <names>.` (or `there are none`).
- `jig presets` prints the same lines as today: name, source label (`repository`, `home`, `xdg`, `builtin`) and path, then the description if any.
- A preset replaces whole roles in the config and never changes run settings.

## Don't undo these

- **`src/cli/with-app.ts` captures the OS home directory and passes it into `parseEnvironment`.** `src/config/` must not call `os.homedir()`; specs rely on this so they never see the real `~/.jig/presets`.
- **The step-retry defaults (2 retries, 5000 ms) live privately in `src/config/load-config.ts`,** and `jig.config.json` and presets reject `maxStepRetries` and `retryDelayMs`. They are configurable defaults that a separate piece of work will expose to operators; don't move them back to `src/domain/` and don't add the override here.
- **Ports in `src/ports/` may import only from `src/domain/`.** If you put the new interfaces in `src/ports/`, they cannot mention `JigConfig` or `Preset`. Declaring them in `src/config/` is fine.
- **`src/config/scratch-directory.ts` (`JIG_DIR = '.jig'`) stays** where it is; other adapters use it. It is out of scope.

## Tighten the dependency rule

Change `config-does-no-io` in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` from a denylist to an allowlist: production files in `src/config/` may import only from `src/config/`, `src/domain/`, `zod` and `better-result`. That forbids `node:path` too, which this work removes from config. Spec files (`*.spec.ts`) may still import test support and `@faker-js/faker`. Update the fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts` so they show an allowed import passing and, for example, `node:path`, `node:child_process` and `execa` being rejected from `src/config/`.

## Tests

Follow `testing-conventions.md`: `setup` not `beforeEach`, fakes over stubs, faker-built data. Config rule specs use a simple in-memory source (a value or a list of candidates), not a fake file system; this should make `FakePresetFiles` in `tests/support/fakes.ts` much smaller or replace it. File-system behaviour (missing files, dangling links, unreadable directories, invalid JSON, atomic writes, the four directories, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) is tested in the adapter's specs with temporary directories.

## Public docs

No operator-facing behaviour changes. Update `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/architecture.html` and `docs/workflow-ownership.md` where they describe config, the config adapters or the dependency rule, so they match the new names and the allowlist. Leave `docs/presets.md` and `docs/configuration.md` alone unless something in them becomes inaccurate.

## How to verify

From the repository root, on the Node version pinned in the repo:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
grep -rnE "node:(fs|os|path)|process\.env|\bpath\b.*from|PresetFiles|ConfigFile\b|configFileFor|mayBeAbsent|PRESET_SOURCES" src/config --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.spec\.ts'
```

The last command must print nothing. Don't run any script that launches an agent on the host or publishes to GitHub or npm.

## Done when

- [ ] `src/config/` production code contains no file-system vocabulary; the grep above prints nothing
- [ ] adapters return raw data and never import `configFrom`, `configWithSettings`, `mayBeAbsent` or any other config rule
- [ ] `config-does-no-io` is an allowlist, with fixtures showing allowed and rejected imports
- [ ] every behaviour listed under "Behaviour that must not change" is still covered by a spec and passes
- [ ] all commands under "How to verify" pass
- [ ] the PR says, for each moved concept, which side owns it now

# test(config): build default configs in specs instead of reading them from disk

**Treat this request as self-contained.** Everything needed is below; don't assume access to any other issue or pull request.

**Start this only after the pull request titled "refactor(config): read settings and presets through sources with no file-system vocabulary" has merged into `main`.** This request relies on files that pull request adds: `tests/support/repository-config.ts`, `InMemoryConfigSource` in `tests/support/fakes.ts`, and `loadConfig(source)` in `src/config/load-config.ts`. If they are not on `main`, stop and report it.

## What

Tests that just need jig's ordinary settings get them directly, instead of creating a scratch folder and reading a settings file from it. Nothing jig does changes; only its tests do.

## Why

About a dozen test files that have nothing to do with how settings are read still go through the real settings-file reader to get the defaults. So every time the way settings are read is reorganised, those unrelated tests change too. That happened twice in a row, and it made two pull requests look much bigger than they were. Tests that need the defaults should depend on the defaults, not on how they are read from disk.

## Context — read this first

jig is a Node/TypeScript CLI, tested with Vitest. Specs sit beside the code they cover. Shared test data builders live in `tests/support/builders.ts` (`runSettings()`, `aRunState()`, `aPreset()` and others), shared fakes in `tests/support/fakes.ts`. Read `.claude/rules/testing-conventions.md` and `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md` before editing.

- `JigConfig` and its defaults are owned by the schema in `src/config/load-config.ts`. `loadConfig(source: ConfigSource)` reads raw JSON from a source, applies the "only an operator-chosen `--config` file must exist" rule, and parses it with that schema.
- `tests/support/fakes.ts` has `InMemoryConfigSource`, a `ConfigSource` that holds JSON in memory. Constructed with no `json`, it reports "absent"; with `custom: false`, an absent source yields the defaults.
- `tests/support/repository-config.ts` exports `repositoryConfig(repoRoot)`, which calls `loadConfig(configFileSource(configDestination(repoRoot)))`: it reads `jig.config.json` from a real directory on disk.

Current callers of `repositoryConfig` (counts are call sites):

| File | Calls |
|---|---|
| `src/app/run-stores.spec.ts` | 11 |
| `src/app/run-jig.spec.ts` | 2 |
| `src/app/run-status.spec.ts` | 2 |
| `src/adapters/sandcastle/open-session.spec.ts` | 1 |
| `src/app/container.spec.ts` | 1 |
| `src/app/sandbox-image.spec.ts` | 1 |
| `src/app/throwaway-sandbox.spec.ts` | 1 |
| `src/integrations/github/implement-issue.spec.ts` | 1 |
| `tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts` | 1 |

`src/app/init-sandbox.spec.ts` (around line 395) inlines the same chain, `unwrap(loadConfig(configFileSource(configDestination(repo.dir))))`, without the helper.

## The change

1. **Add `aJigConfig(overrides: Partial<JigConfig> = {})` to `tests/support/builders.ts`.** It returns the defaults with `overrides` spread over them. Get the defaults from the real schema, by calling `loadConfig` with an `InMemoryConfigSource` that is absent and not custom. **Don't restate any default value in the builder.** The schema owns them, and a copy would drift.
2. **Replace each call site that only needs a default config** with `aJigConfig()`, or `aJigConfig({ runStores })` and similar where the spec spreads overrides today (`{ ...repositoryConfig(repoRoot), runStores }` becomes `aJigConfig({ runStores })`).
3. **Keep the disk read where reading the repository's file is the point.** Before replacing a call, check whether the spec (or its setup) writes a `jig.config.json` into the directory, or asserts something that depends on the file on disk. If it does, the spec is testing that the repository's settings are honoured: keep `repositoryConfig` there. `tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts` is an end-to-end test of a real repository; keep its disk read. List every call site you kept in the PR, with the reason.
4. **If no call site still needs `repositoryConfig`, delete `tests/support/repository-config.ts`.** Otherwise leave it for the ones that do.
5. Where a spec's temporary directory existed only to produce a config, and nothing else in that spec uses it, remove the directory too. Don't remove a directory the code under test still needs, for example as a repository root.

## Don't undo these

- **Config defaults live only in the schema in `src/config/load-config.ts`.** The builder asks the schema; it never copies values. That includes the step retry defaults (2 retries, 5000 ms), which are private constants there and are not part of `JigConfig`.
- **Specs for reading settings from disk stay on disk.** The specs of `src/adapters/filesystem/config-source.ts` and `src/config/load-config.ts` test reading and parsing; don't switch them to the builder.
- **Follow `testing-conventions.md`:** `setup` not `beforeEach`, faker-built data where a value doesn't matter, no module mocks.

## Public docs

None. This changes tests only.

## How to verify

From the repository root, on the Node version pinned in the repo:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
grep -rn "repositoryConfig\|configFileSource(configDestination" src tests --include=*.spec.ts
```

The grep must list only the call sites the PR names as kept, with reasons. Don't run any script that launches an agent on the host or publishes to GitHub or npm.

## Done when

- [ ] `aJigConfig()` exists in `tests/support/builders.ts` and takes its defaults from the schema, with no default values written in it
- [ ] every spec that only needs a default config uses `aJigConfig`; each remaining disk read is listed in the PR with why it stays
- [ ] no file under `src/` other than specs changed
- [ ] all commands under "How to verify" pass

# refactor(domain): assign error ownership by meaning

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Lands after the issue that splits config I/O from config policy, and builds on it.

## What

Every kind of failure jig reports has a clear owner. Users see the same error messages, and the
same failures are retried, blocked or fatal.

## Why

All failures live in one domain file, together with error helpers and retry execution. Business
code therefore appears to depend on storage, Git and configuration details, and each new failure
type adds to a single global list.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec section: "Error ownership and technical failure handling".

- `src/domain/errors.ts` (220 lines) holds the `JigError` union, `FailureKind`, `isTransient`,
  `isJigError`, `messageOf`, `rootCause` and 21 error classes: `AgentRunFailed`,
  `AgentOutputInvalid`, `PlanNotCovered`, `DesignUnresolved`, `RemoteUnavailable`,
  `SandboxUnavailable`, `SetupCommandFailed`, `RunStateConflict`, `RunCodeUnavailable`,
  `MergeFailed`, `GitCommandFailed`, `CommitImportRefused`, `CommitRejected`, `ConfigInvalid`,
  `RunRequestInvalid`, `RunInProgress`, `MetricsLogCorrupt`, `LocalStateUnwritable`,
  `CodexLoginNotSaved`, `ImageBuildFailed`, `CommandInputInvalid`.
- `src/domain/retry.ts` combines the transient-error policy with retry execution.
- `src/integrations/github/errors.ts` holds GitHub-specific errors; leave them for the GitHub issue
  unless a shared class is involved.

Ownership:

- Domain keeps business failures, such as `PlanNotCovered` and `DesignUnresolved`.
- Ports own capability failures (storage, Git, sandbox), defined once, without raw library details.
- Config owns configuration-validation failures. **`ConfigInvalid` appears in `RunStoreFailure`
  (`src/ports/run-store.ts`)**: moving it into config unchanged would make ports depend on config.
  First list what it actually means at each use, then split it or define the portable contract
  below its consumers.
- CLI owns transport input failures (`CommandInputInvalid`). App owns use-case failures.
- Adapters translate raw third-party exceptions into the declared capability failures.

Before moving anything, list the consumers of each helper and separate four things: what an error
means, retry/block/fatal classification, presentation and unwrapping (`messageOf`, `rootCause`),
and retry execution. Use better-result facilities instead of rebuilding them. Keep a thin wrapper
only where it preserves behavior the library lacks, and say which behavior in the PR. Use narrow
unions where a decision is exhaustive. An aggregate union may live at the application boundary
that needs it; domain and flow must not import it. Flow's failure type comes from the steps and
stores it calls. Remove registry machinery that nothing uses instead of moving it.

Do not create a top-level `failures` or shared-utilities owner. If the inventory shows that one is
needed, stop and propose its responsibility, consumers and allowed dependency edges in the PR
description before building it.

## Done when

- [ ] The PR contains a table listing every error's old owner, new owner, and how its tag, fields
      and retry/block/fatal classification are preserved at its consumers.
- [ ] Domain imports no capability, config or CLI error. Ports import nothing outside domain and ports.
- [ ] No moved error creates an outward import or a cycle (`npm run lint:dependencies`).
- [ ] Behavior tests show unchanged classification and user-visible messages, including
      original-cause reporting.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.

# refactor(domain): move shared failure helpers into a failures owner

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**:
everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to
any other issue or pull request.

Lands before the issue that assigns error classes to their owners; that issue builds on this one.

## What

The small pieces of code that describe a failure and retry a failed step get a home of their own.
Users see the same messages, and the same steps are retried the same number of times.

## Why

Those pieces live with the business rules today, although they are not business rules. They are
used from almost every part of jig, and no other existing place can be reached from all of those
parts. Giving them one dedicated place lets the business rules stay pure.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, files, containers, terminal, logging), `integrations/github`, `app` (use cases)
and `cli` (commands). Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before
editing, read `AGENTS.md`, the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and
`docs/architecture.html`.

Read these sections of `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`: "Target responsibilities" (the
owner table and the `failures` paragraphs below it) and "Error ownership and technical failure
handling". Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow the spec and say so in the PR.

## Target

A new owner, `src/failures/`. It imports no project source; it depends only on `better-result` and
Node. Callers import its functions directly.

Move these, with their specs, and change nothing about how they behave:

| Today | Moves to | Consumers today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageOf` in `src/domain/errors.ts` | `src/failures/messages.ts` | adapters (filesystem, find-symlink, git, local-store, run-store, sandbox-image, sandcastle, terminal), `app/init-sandbox.ts`, `app/run-stores.ts`, `app/sandbox-image.ts`, `cli/read-request.ts`, `cli/with-error-handling.ts`, `flow/engine.ts`, `observers/run-events.ts`, `integrations/github` |
| `rootCause` in `src/domain/errors.ts` | `src/failures/messages.ts` | `flow/engine.ts`, `cli/with-error-handling.ts` |
| `retryResult`, `RetryPolicy` in `src/domain/retry.ts` | `src/failures/retry.ts` | `adapters/git/remote-ref.ts`, `app/container.ts`, `flow/engine.ts`, `steps/planning.ts`, `integrations/github/octokit-github.ts`, `integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts` |

Grep for each name before you start; the table is a starting point, not a substitute.

Stays in `domain`, untouched by this issue: every error class, `JigError`, `FailureKind`,
`isTransient`, `isJigError`, and `transientRetryPolicy`. `transientRetryPolicy(settings)` reads
`RunSettings` and returns `{ retries, delayMs, shouldRetry: isTransient }`. Domain must not import
`failures`, so type its result structurally in `src/domain/retry.ts`; it still satisfies
`RetryPolicy` at the call site. A separate issue moves the error classes; do not start that here.

`retryResult` stays a hand-written wrapper. better-result 3.0.1's retry exists only inside
`Result.tryPromise`, which retries a rejected promise. jig operations return `Result` values and
never throw, and callers need `onFailedAttempt` on every failed attempt, the last one included.
Keep exactly this: the first attempt runs at once; `onFailedAttempt({ error, attempt, retriesLeft })`
runs before the retry decision, including the final and non-retryable attempt; the delay is
`delayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`; the last `Err` is returned. Never throw an `Err` to reach a library
retry loop. Say this in the PR as the reason for the wrapper.

## Dependency rules

Policy lives in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with fixtures in
`scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.

- Add `failures` to `productionModules` in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`.
- `failures` imports nothing under `src/` outside `src/failures/`.
- `domain`, `ports`, `config` and `prompts` do not import `failures`.
- Every other owner may import it. `integrations/github` keeps its current imports until the GitHub
  issue moves it.
- Add a passing and a failing fixture for each rule.

## Don't undo these

- **No port, adapter or injection for these helpers.** Do not add `src/ports/retry.ts`,
  `src/ports/exception-details.ts` or adapter implementations of them, and do not pass them through
  constructors, dependency objects or the container. They are pure functions (plus a timer); a
  direct import is the design.
- Do not change construction or wiring in `src/app/container.ts` beyond its import paths. The
  construction mechanism is decided separately.
- No compatibility re-exports from `src/domain/errors.ts` or `src/domain/retry.ts`. Update every
  caller.
- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Change only what this issue needs. Leave unrelated specs and assertions as they are.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.

## Documentation

Internal-only work: no public guide changes. Update these references in place, present tense:

- `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`: the paths for `rootCause` and `retryResult`, and the
  paragraph that says the panic helpers live in `src/domain/errors.ts`.
- `docs/architecture.html`: the failure-policy card that names `retryResult` and `domain`, plus
  any owner list.
- `docs/workflow-ownership.md`: import lines that now point at `failures/`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: add `src/failures/` to the code map.

## How to work

From the repository root, with Node 26.13.0:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

## Done when

- [ ] `git grep -n -E "export (async )?function (messageOf|rootCause|retryResult)" src` finds them
      only under `src/failures/`
- [ ] `git grep -n "from '.*failures/" src/domain src/ports src/config src/prompts` finds nothing
- [ ] `src/ports/retry.ts` and `src/ports/exception-details.ts` do not exist
- [ ] the specs for `messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` pass from their new location, with
      the same cases as before
- [ ] `npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation` passes from the repository root
- [ ] the PR names `failures` as the owner, says why these helpers belong there, and says it is a
      one-off: new helpers go to the module whose rule they express, not here by habit


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/68

# refactor(domain): assign error ownership by meaning

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**:
everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to
any other issue or pull request.

Lands after two earlier issues and builds on both: the one that splits config I/O from config
policy, and the one that moves `messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` into `src/failures/`.
Check that `src/failures/` exists before you start; if it does not, stop and say so.

## What

Every kind of failure jig reports has a clear owner. Users see the same error messages, and the
same failures are retried, blocked or fatal.

## Why

All failures live in one domain file. Business code therefore appears to depend on storage, Git and
configuration details, and each new failure type adds to a single global list.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `failures` (failure presentation, unwrapping and retry execution),
`ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and policy), `flow`/`steps`
(workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting), `adapters` (Git, files,
containers, terminal, logging), `integrations/github`, `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

Read these sections of `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`: "Target responsibilities" and "Error
ownership and technical failure handling". Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow the spec
and say so in the PR.

## Target

`src/domain/errors.ts` holds the `JigError` union, `FailureKind`, `isTransient`, `isJigError` and
21 error classes. Move each class to the owner of the condition it describes, split
`ConfigInvalid` by meaning, and replace `JigError` with narrow contracts. Do the two required first
steps below before moving any class.

**Out of scope:** `messageOf`, `rootCause`, `retryResult` and `RetryPolicy`. They already live in
`src/failures/`; import them from there and do not move, wrap or inject them.
`src/integrations/github/errors.ts` holds GitHub-specific errors; leave them for the GitHub issue
unless a shared class is involved.

### Step 1 (required first): find every place an error tag is read, shown or stored

Each class split out of `ConfigInvalid` gets its own tag (see `ConfigInvalid` below). Before
changing any tag, grep `src/` for every read of `_tag`, every match on the string `'ConfigInvalid'`,
every `instanceof` or class-name check, and every place an error is serialized or logged. For each
one, decide whether a tag change there is visible to users or breaks stored data, and put the list
in the PR. An earlier read-only investigation found the following; confirm it against the code as
it stands, since lines may have moved.

Production code that reads a jig error tag. None of these involve `ConfigInvalid`, so the split
does not affect them:

- `src/adapters/git/remote-ref.ts:57` retries when `_tag === 'RemoteUnavailable'`.
- `src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:137,140` retries and recovers on
  `_tag === 'RunStateConflict'`.
- `src/integrations/github/octokit-github.ts:62` and `implement-issue.ts:473` match GitHub's own
  tags (`GithubUnavailable`, `GithubRefused`).
- `src/config/presets.ts:51` switches on `PresetSourceFailure` tags.
- `src/adapters/sandcastle/sandcastle-session.ts:311-320` reads sandcastle's own failure tags to
  decide between `ConfigInvalid` and `SandboxUnavailable`. That tag set belongs to the library.
  The class it produces changes; nothing reads jig's tag there.

No production code compares against the string `'ConfigInvalid'` or uses
`instanceof ConfigInvalid`. Classification uses `kind` (`src/flow/engine.ts:226`), not the tag.

Surfaces that show or store errors:

| Surface | What it carries | Tag change visible or breaking? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI output and exit code (`src/cli/with-error-handling.ts:22`) | an `Err`'s `message` only; every `Err` exits 1 | No |
| Saved run state, local and remote (`blockedReason`, `src/flow/engine.ts:227`) | the error's `message` | No |
| Run events and metrics log (`reason` in `src/domain/events.ts`, `src/observers/metrics.ts:27,86`) | the error's `message` | No |
| GitHub orchestration state and comments (`src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:159`) | statuses and receipts, no errors | No |
| Telemetry (`src/observers/tracing-observer.ts:31,81`) | span status message from `reason` | No |
| Logs written with `{ err }` (`src/app/report-cleanup.ts:12`, `src/app/observed-events.ts:13`, `src/app/throwaway-sandbox.ts:61`, `src/adapters/sandcastle/sandcastle-session.ts:342,370`) | pino's error serializer writes `type` (the constructor name), `message`, `stack` and own fields, including `_tag`; `TaggedError` also sets `name` to the tag, so the stack starts with it | Visible in the console and the run's JSON log file, but only as diagnostics: nothing in jig parses them, and `type` changes with the class anyway |
| Specs | 56 `toBeInstanceOf(ConfigInvalid)` assertions across 22 spec files; `src/domain/errors.spec.ts:105` asserts `_tag === constructor.name` for every class | Instance assertions must name the new classes. The tag-equals-class-name test already requires distinct tags; keep it and extend it to the new classes |

Conclusion of that investigation: **no surface needs a compatibility translation.** Log lines show
the new tags, and that change is accepted. If you find a surface that shows the tag to users as
part of a stable output, or stores it in data that jig reads back, keep compatibility at that one
point with an explicit translation from the new tag to `'ConfigInvalid'`, and name it in the PR.

### Step 2 (required early): move retry-policy assembly from domain to flow

Retry counts and delays are technical policy, not business rules. Step retry has three owners:

- Config owns the defaults: `STEP_RETRIES = 2` and `STEP_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5000` in
  `src/config/load-config.ts`, copied by `runSettingsFrom` into `RunSettings.maxStepRetries` and
  `retryDelayMs`. Leave them there. Domain keeps the resolved `RunSettings` type.
- Classification stays with the errors: each class keeps its literal `kind`, and domain keeps
  `FailureKind` and `isTransient` as a plain rule (see "Classification" below).
- Flow owns assembling the `RetryPolicy`, because flow makes the step retry decision.

Today `transientRetryPolicy(settings: RunSettings)` returns
`{ retries: settings.maxStepRetries, delayMs: settings.retryDelayMs, shouldRetry: isTransient }`,
and its consumers are `src/flow/engine.ts` and `src/app/container.ts`. The earlier helper move may
have left it in `src/domain/retry.ts` with a structural result type that copies `RetryPolicy`'s
shape so domain need not import `failures`. Check where `transientRetryPolicy` and its result type
live when you start, and move them from there:

- Put the builder in flow, for example `src/flow/retry-policy.ts`. It imports `RetryPolicy` from
  `src/failures/retry.ts` and returns that type, not a lookalike.
- `src/flow/engine.ts` imports it from flow. `src/app/container.ts` imports it from flow too; the
  owner table allows app to import flow.
- Remove the builder and the structural lookalike type from domain. Delete `src/domain/retry.ts`
  if nothing is left in it.
- Move its specs with it. Same retries, same delays, same retryable kinds. No new settings.

### Proposed owners — verify each against its callers

A starting proposal from an earlier inventory. Every class in this table keeps its tag, message
and literal `kind`; only the classes split out of `ConfigInvalid` below get new tags. Check each row against the actual constructors and consumers; where a caller shows a
different meaning, follow the caller and record why in the PR.

| Error | Owner | Extra fields | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AgentRunFailed` | `ports/agent-session` | — | retry |
| `AgentOutputInvalid` | `ports/agent-session` | — | retry |
| `PlanNotCovered` | `domain/errors` | — | retry |
| `DesignUnresolved` | `domain/errors` | `findingIds` | block |
| `RemoteUnavailable` | `ports/git` | — | retry |
| `SandboxUnavailable` | `ports/sandbox-session` | — | retry |
| `SetupCommandFailed` | `ports/sandbox-session` | `output` | retry |
| `RunStateConflict` | `ports/run-state-failures` | — | block |
| `RunCodeUnavailable` | `ports/run-code` | — | block |
| `MergeFailed` | `ports/workspace` | — | block |
| `GitCommandFailed` | `ports/git` | `command`, `output` | block |
| `CommitImportRefused` | `ports/workspace` | — | block |
| `CommitRejected` | `ports/workspace` | `output` | block |
| `ConfigInvalid` | `config/errors`, split below | — | fatal |
| `RunRequestInvalid` | `app/run-request` | — | fatal |
| `RunInProgress` | `ports/run-lock` | — | fatal |
| `MetricsLogCorrupt` | `ports/metrics-log` | — | fatal |
| `LocalStateUnwritable` | `ports/local-state` | `path` | fatal |
| `CodexLoginNotSaved` | `ports/sandbox-session` | — | fatal |
| `ImageBuildFailed` | `ports/sandbox-images` | `output` | fatal |
| `CommandInputInvalid` | `cli/errors` | — | fatal |

Shared Git failures live once in `ports/git.ts`. Shared run-state failures live in
`ports/run-state-failures.ts`, which `run-store` and `run-code` both import, so neither imports the
other. No ports-wide error barrel and no re-exports from `domain`.

### `ConfigInvalid`

`ConfigInvalid` appears in `RunStoreFailure` (`src/ports/run-store.ts`), so moving it into config
unchanged would make ports depend on config. Keep `ConfigInvalid` in config for schema,
environment, preset and provider-selection validation only. Proposed splits for its other uses:

| Meaning today | Replacement and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid local or remote saved run; invalid state from a custom store | `RunStateInvalid`, `ports/run-state-failures` |
| Custom-store operational failure | `RunStoreOperationFailed`, `ports/run-store` |
| Loading or validating a custom-store module | `RunStoreSetupInvalid`, `app/run-stores` |
| Missing credentials, invalid selected login, credential-file access | `SandboxCredentialsInvalid`, `ports/sandbox-session` |
| Sandbox setup prerequisites or recipe validation | `SandboxPreparationInvalid`, `ports/sandbox-session` |
| Repository, root or branch prerequisites | `RepositoryInvalid`, `ports/git` |
| Symlink refusal and prerequisite file operations outside config sources | `LocalPreparationFailed`, `ports/local-state` |

Each replacement gets its own `_tag`, equal to its class name (`RunStateInvalid`,
`RunStoreOperationFailed`, and so on), so no two classes share a tag and a tag can be matched
exhaustively. Each keeps the message-only payload, the same message text and `kind: 'fatal'`, so
users see the same output and exit code. Use step 1's list for the tag checks, `instanceof`,
class-name checks and serialization to update; add a compatibility translation only where step 1
says one is needed. Keep the prerequisite cases that are deliberately
translated into `MergeFailed`. Config keeps its current import allowlist; adapters translate config
validation into capability failures where needed.

### Classification and workflow contracts

- Classes keep their literal `kind`. Domain keeps `FailureKind` and `isTransient`, which takes the
  structural input `{ kind: FailureKind }` instead of `JigError`. The flow retry-policy builder from
  step 2 uses it as `shouldRetry`.
- Replace `JigError` in `src/flow/define-flow.ts` and `src/flow/engine.ts` with step failures built
  from domain and port failures, plus each engine method's persistence failures. Flow must not
  import `steps` or `app` to derive these types (lint rule `flow-does-not-assemble-workflows`).
  `app` checks that the assembled workflow fits flow's contracts.
- Remove `JigError`. Define an aggregate only at an application operation that needs one, and keep
  CLI-only errors out of it.
- Delete `isJigError` and its class registry; nothing in production uses them.

## Don't undo these

- **`messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` stay in `src/failures/` as direct imports.** Do not
  add ports, adapters or injection for them. The same applies to the flow retry-policy builder: it
  is an ordinary function that engine and app import, not a port or a dependency passed in.
- Do not change construction or wiring in `src/app/container.ts` beyond import paths and types.
  The construction mechanism is decided separately.
- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged. The one tag change is the distinct tags of the
  classes split out of `ConfigInvalid`; their messages and exit codes stay the same.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- Change only what this issue needs. Leave unrelated specs and assertions as they are.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.

## Documentation

Internal-only work: no public guide changes. Update these references in place, present tense:
`docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
`.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md` (the paragraph about where classes live today, which also says
the move "keeps every tag": say instead that split classes get their own tags), and any other file
that names a moved path or `transientRetryPolicy`.

## Verification

From the repository root, with Node 26.13.0:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub.

## Done when

- [ ] The PR has a table with every error's old owner, new owner, and how its tag, fields and
      retry/block/fatal classification are kept at its consumers.
- [ ] `git grep -n -w -e JigError -e isJigError src` finds nothing.
- [ ] No two error classes share a `_tag`: every class's tag equals its class name, as
      `src/domain/errors.spec.ts` (or wherever its cases move) checks for every class, the new
      ones included.
- [ ] The PR lists step 1's tag read/show/store places and says which, if any, needed a
      compatibility translation.
- [ ] Domain exports no retry-policy builder and no retry-policy type:
      `git grep -n -E "export .*(RetryPolicy|transientRetryPolicy)" src/domain` finds nothing.
- [ ] The flow builder returns `RetryPolicy` imported from `src/failures/retry.ts`, and
      `src/flow/engine.ts` and `src/app/container.ts` import the builder from flow.
- [ ] Domain imports no capability, config or CLI error. Ports import nothing outside domain and
      ports (`npm run lint:dependencies`).
- [ ] Behavior tests show unchanged classification and messages, including retries running out and
      becoming blocked with the same count and delays, immediate blocking, fatal propagation,
      malformed saved state and original-cause reporting.
- [ ] The verification above passes.



Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/56

# refactor(cli): introduce the composition owner and executable

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Lands after the error-ownership issue, and builds on it. The next slices (moving the GitHub code,
then the application API) build on this one and also edit `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`.

## What

The `jig` command starts from one clearly named place that does nothing except assemble the
program and start it. Commands, help and installed usage behave exactly as before.

## Why

Startup and wiring currently live inside the GitHub feature folder, which makes that folder an
extra layer above the command line. A dedicated starting point keeps wiring separate from command
handling and application behavior.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Composition", "Dependency lint", and the `composition` row of "Target responsibilities".

- `src/integrations/github/cli.ts` composes the full CLI and starts the executable. Move executable
  startup and command composition to `src/composition/main.ts`, keeping the realpath check that
  makes installed symlinks work. Importing builders or the module must not start a command.
- `package.json`: `bin.jig`, `main` (`./dist/integrations/github/cli.js`) and `scripts.dev`
  (`tsx src/integrations/github/cli.ts`) point at the new executable. Update path-sensitive tests,
  `tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts`, and `docs/installation.md` line 52.
- Composition may import `app`, `cli`, `adapters`, `config`, `observers`, `ports` and `domain`.
  It only chooses implementations, constructs them and starts the executable. In this slice it
  still calls the existing app container. Leave the container itself alone; a separate spike
  decides how it changes.
- Dependency Cruiser: add `composition` to `productionModules` in `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`.
  Add the rules "only composition imports `src/cli/` from another owner" and "no other owner
  imports `src/composition/`". The rules cover type-only imports, re-exports and literal dynamic
  imports. `scripts/validate.ts` may keep using CLI parsing helpers; do not let the source-only
  rule break it. Extend `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts` with fixtures that accept composition
  importing CLI and reject an adapter, app or nested file importing CLI or composition. Each
  rejection must fail under the named rule, not because of an incidental cycle.
- `src/integrations/github/command.ts` remains a CLI-side command file; the next slice moves it.
  If a temporary edge from `cli` to `integrations` is needed, record it in the PR and do not add a
  forwarding module.

## Done when

- [ ] `node dist/composition/main.js --help` and `node dist/composition/main.js github implement --help`
      work after `npm run build`, and a symlinked executable starts.
- [ ] A spec imports the composition builders without starting a command.
- [ ] Fixtures prove the new rules, including type-only, re-export, dynamic, nested and
      disconnected offenders.
- [ ] Executable paths in `package.json`, the tests and the docs point at `src/composition/main.ts`.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/57
